entry.title: Figma employee sues, alleging company forced her to confront harassers
entry.summary: Figma and its CEO are being sued by a current employee for alleged sexual harassment and discrimination.

entry.title: Huang reportedly admitted to more than two affairs to Nvidia’s board
entry.summary: During a meeting before his reinstatement, Huang admitted to more affairs beyond the two that have been reported in the news, according to The Wall Street Journal.

entry.title: Amazon’s Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the silicon gap with Nvidia
entry.summary: Amazon’s decision to acquire Decart for a reported $7.5 billion is part of its efforts to improve the efficiency of its Trainium chips.

entry.title: Pinterest will now let parents limit the AI-generated content their teens see
entry.summary: While other social platforms have focused on restricting teens' access to AI chatbots, Pinterest is addressing the AI content filling their feeds.

entry.title: Why a Crusoe investor is betting on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers
entry.summary: Next-generation data centers will need tens of gigawatts of power every year. One of Crusoe's investors thinks solar and energy storage are the obvious choice.

entry.title: Uber and Nuro begin driverless testing of Lucid robotaxis ahead of 2027 launch
entry.summary: Uber and Nuro have started testing driverless Lucid Gravity SUVs on public streets in the San Francisco Bay Area.

entry.title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming
entry.summary: The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.

entry.title: Meta brings its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram DMs
entry.summary: The new integration gets rid of the need for users to toggle between Instagram and the Muse app when they want to interact with the AI agent.

entry.title: Electric truck startup Harbinger gets financing boost from Palmer Luckey’s bank
entry.summary: Harbinger has tapped Palmer Luckey's Erebor Bank as a new source of capital as the electric truck startup looks to diversify how it funds its growth.

entry.title: Threads comes to iPad and takes a page from X’s playbook with cashtags
entry.summary: The addition of live stock quotes and charts could help Threads attract the financial community that has historically relied on X.

entry.title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security
entry.summary: The British cyber agency says that "building strong foundations has never mattered more" as AI hacking tools rely on exploiting simple security flaws.

entry.title: Anthropic shares fall below IPO price, a worrying sign for AI startups
entry.summary: Anthropic’s post-IPO slump could put pressure on AI startup valuations.

entry.title: Dozens of oil and shipping tankers hacked in recent weeks, per report
entry.summary: Iran is the chief suspect behind the dozens of cyberattacks targeting oil and chemical shipping vessels.

entry.title: Maple raises $5.3M to build AI products that protect your data, even from itself
entry.summary: The startup's encrypted AI architecture is designed to prevent even the company itself from accessing users' private data.

entry.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse
entry.summary: Walmart now lets customers shop Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent.

entry.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life
entry.summary: As millions embrace personal AI assistants, a new benchmark reveals that even the most advanced AI models struggle to complete everyday tasks reliably and safely without introducing potential new problems.

entry.title: In all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang thanks White House and says he’s in therapy
entry.summary: The Nvidia founder apologized to his staff on Tuesday and said he was grateful for a second chance to lead the company.

entry.title: Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy
entry.summary: It's a remarkable stance for a company that spent the last two weeks finding out what happens without its founder.

entry.title: Trump reportedly says pardoning Jensen Huang is ‘an option’
entry.summary: The New York Post says that, in an exclusive interview, the President said that pardoning the Nvidia co-founder is "an option," but not one that he thought he would need to use.

entry.title: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to U.S. industrial might — not a champion
entry.summary: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld warns that what the market cheered Monday, Jensen Huang's White House–backed return as Nvidia's CEO and board member, could prove a giant mistake, exposing the directors to "historic" personal liability from a growing pile of lawsuits and raising the question of whether the country is celebrating a company that has helped put advanced chips in its adversaries' hands.
